chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zurārah, from ʿĪsā ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Hāshimī, from his grandfather, from ʿAlī عليه السلام, who said:
ʿAlī عليه السلام and ʿUmar entered the bathhouse, and ʿUmar said: “How evil a house the bathhouse is; hardship is abundant in it, and modesty is little in it.”
So ʿAlī عليه السلام said: “How excellent a house the bathhouse is: it removes filth and brings the Fire to mind.”

key_terms.الْأَذَى: filth, harm, or impurity removed by bathing
key_terms.الْحَمَّامُ: the bathhouse; a place of washing and cleansing
key_terms.الْعَنَاءُ: hardship or discomfort found in such a place
key_terms.بِالنَّارِ: the Fire, meaning hellfire, as a reminder for reflection

ai.seo_question: What did Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام say about entering the bathhouse?
ai.summary: This hadith presents Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام giving a balanced moral view of the bathhouse. While it may be a place where modesty is reduced, he emphasizes its benefits: removing bodily harm and reminding one of the Fire, making it a source of both cleanliness and reflection.
